<awtsmoosMeluketTranslation heichel="ikar" alias="meluket_translation_en" seriesId="סיון_meluket" postId="BH_POST_1766518918811_theRebbe_734" batchId="meluket-_D7_A1_D7_99_D7_95_D7_9F_meluket__BH_POST_1766518918811_theRebbe_734__p003">
  <section v="6">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>This section explains that just as in the flow of influence, so too in action, the end of action is the deed itself, and the root of the deed is in the beginning—pleasure—while the revelation of pleasure is specifically in the deed, culminating in the craftsman's pleasure in the successful, beautiful outcome.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">And just as31 it is regarding the flow of influence, so too is it in all of action,</t>
    <t s="1">that their end is the action itself,</t>
    <t s="2">the making and doing of man,</t>
    <t s="3">and it is called by the name "their end,"</t>
    <t s="4">for the power of deed is the most ultimate power,</t>
    <t s="5">and also the activity of the deed comes at the end.</t>
    <t s="6">For first is the pleasure,</t>
    <t s="7">and from this are drawn will, intellect, and the emotions,</t>
    <t s="8">and the emotions are clothed in thought and speech,</t>
    <t s="9">and afterward comes the deed32.</t>
    <t s="10">And their end is interwoven in their beginning, and their beginning in their end,</t>
    <t s="11">for the root of the deed is in the pleasure,</t>
    <t s="12">which is the "beginning,"</t>
    <t s="13">the cause of the will and the other faculties.</t>
    <t s="14">And likewise their beginning is interwoven in their end,</t>
    <t s="15">for the revelation of pleasure is specifically in the deed.</t>
    <t s="16">And the end of the deed is</t>
    <t s="17">(not the action itself,</t>
    <t s="18">but rather)</t>
    <t s="19">the deed that is done through the making and doing of man.</t>
    <t s="20">And the main point of the end of the deed is in the deed that comes through his doing, which is not dependent on man's will.</t>
    <t s="21">And like a craftsman who does work,</t>
    <t s="22">that the fact that the craftsman cannot take upon himself that the work will be successful</t>
    <t s="23">[for this matter is not dependent on the craftsman.</t>
    <t s="24">And it is in the manner explained above regarding the reception of influence,</t>
    <t s="25">that this depends on the recipient and not on the giver].</t>
    <t s="26">And the end of the deed is in thought at first,</t>
    <t s="27">that the pleasure of the craftsman from the fact that the work is done with utmost splendor and beauty</t>
    <t s="28">(in a manner of success)</t>
    <t s="29">is a pleasure more elevated than the pleasure in the doing of the work.</t>
    <t s="30">For the pleasure that the work is done is a composite pleasure</t>
    <t s="31">(pleasure from the doing of the work),</t>
    <t s="32">and by his seeing that the work is done with splendor and beauty,</t>
    <t s="33">the simple pleasure is revealed</t>
    <t s="34">(as explained in the continuation above).</t>
  </section>
  <section v="7">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>This section discusses that the two aspects of action—man's doing and the resulting deed—have parallels in man's own action, where the root of the clothing of faculties in deed is in the soul's revealed aspect, while the root of the deed itself is in the soul's essence, analogous to "the end of the deed is in thought at first."</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">5)</t>
    <t s="1">And it is known33</t>
    <t s="2">that the superiority of man begins from the power of speech within him34</t>
    <t s="3">(unlike deed, which also exists in animals).</t>
    <t s="4">And based on this, it can be said,</t>
    <t s="5">that the two matters in deed—the making and doing of man</t>
    <t s="6">(their end),</t>
    <t s="7">and the deed that comes through his doing</t>
    <t s="8">(the end of the deed)</t>
    <t s="9">—there are</t>
    <t s="10">(their parallels)</t>
    <t s="11">also in the action of man.</t>
    <t s="12">For that the faculties of man</t>
    <t s="13">(intellect, emotions, thought, and speech)</t>
    <t s="14">are drawn and clothed in the deed,</t>
    <t s="15">is in the manner of the making and doing of man,</t>
    <t s="16">and the deed itself</t>
    <t s="17">(as it is separate from the faculties above it,</t>
    <t s="18">which are the essence of man)</t>
    <t s="19">is in the manner of the deed</t>
    <t s="20">(that is outside of man)</t>
    <t s="21">that is done through the making and doing of man.</t>
    <t s="22">And the distinction between the two matters in their root in the soul is,</t>
    <t s="23">that the root of the deed that pertains to the faculties above it</t>
    <t s="24">(i.e., the clothing of the faculties in the deed)</t>
    <t s="25">is in the aspect of the revelation of the soul.</t>
    <t s="26">And that is35,</t>
    <t s="27">that also the root of this matter in the deed is in the soul that is above the faculties.</t>
    <t s="28">For the faculties in themselves are separate and it is not within their capacity to descend so low and to be clothed in deed,</t>
    <t s="29">and that it is possible for them to descend and be clothed in deed is through that which is drawn into them from the soul</t>
    <t s="30">(which is above the faculties),</t>
    <t s="31">which is present in all the faculties and limbs equally.</t>
    <t s="32">But this matter in the soul</t>
    <t s="33">(that it has the capacity to descend very low)</t>
    <t s="34">is the aspect of its revelation—in the manner of "their end is interwoven in their beginning,"</t>
    <t s="35">that the root of "their end"</t>
    <t s="36">(the doing of man)</t>
    <t s="37">is in the "beginning,"</t>
    <t s="38">the root of influence.</t>
    <t s="39">And the root of the deed itself</t>
    <t s="40">(as it is separate from the faculties above it)</t>
    <t s="41">is in the essence of the soul35</t>
    <t s="42">—in the manner of "the end of the deed is in thought at first,"</t>
    <t s="43">that the root of the end of the deed</t>
    <t s="44">(that is outside of man)</t>
    <t s="45">is in the beginning that precedes the beginning of thought,</t>
    <t s="46">above the root of influence.</t>
  </section>
  <section v="8">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>This section explains that in the superiority of deed where the soul's limitless aspect is revealed through the clothing of intellect and emotions in deed, the intellect precedes the deed, but in the superiority of deed from the perspective of its root in the soul's essence, the deed precedes all faculties, as seen in "we will do and we will hear" and Yehudah offering before Yissachar.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">And it can be said,</t>
    <t s="1">that in the superiority of the deed in that through it the limitless aspect of the soul is revealed—the intellect and emotions etc. are before</t>
    <t s="2">[and above]</t>
    <t s="3">the deed.</t>
    <t s="4">For since the revelation of the limitless aspect of the soul is that the intellect and emotions are drawn and clothed in the deed,</t>
    <t s="5">behold, the intellect and emotions precede the deed.</t>
    <t s="6">And also above the deed.</t>
    <t s="7">For the superiority of deed</t>
    <t s="8">(in this aspect)</t>
    <t s="9">is not in the deed itself but in that the intellect and emotions are clothed in the deed</t>
    <t s="10">[And based on this, it can be explained what they said: "Study is greater, for it brings to deed"</t>
    <t s="11">(for at first glance,</t>
    <t s="12">from this very fact that the greatness of study is that it brings to deed, it is proven that the deed is primary,</t>
    <t s="13">and nevertheless study is greater than deed),</t>
    <t s="14">for the advantage of deed over study in this level is that study brings to deed</t>
    <t s="15">(for that study brings to deed is through the drawing into it of the limitless aspect that is above study itself),</t>
    <t s="16">therefore study is greater].</t>
    <t s="17">And in the superiority of the deed from the aspect that the root of the deed itself is in the essence of the soul—the deed is before</t>
    <t s="18">(and above)</t>
    <t s="19">all the faculties,</t>
    <t s="20">and this is that before the giving of the Torah they prioritized "we will do" over "we will hear,"</t>
    <t s="21">and likewise in the dedication of the Mishkan, Yehudah offered</t>
    <t s="22">(deed)</t>
    <t s="23">before Yissachar</t>
    <t s="24">(study),</t>
    <t s="25">for at the giving of the Torah and the establishment of the Mishkan there was the drawing down of the Awtsmoos,</t>
    <t s="26">and there—the deed precedes study.</t>
  </section>
</awtsmoosMeluketTranslation>
